next_state_election.name: General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — 2026 November General Election

glance_notes.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — November 3, 2026 Election Law Calendar
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: Texas's voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is October 5. The ordinary 30-day deadline falls on Sunday, October 4, so state law extends the deadline to the next business day.

glance_notes.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — Early Voting FAQs
glance_notes.text: Early Voting October 19–30: Any registered Texas voter may vote early in person without providing a reason. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting by personal appearance begins October 19 and ends October 30.

glance_notes.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — Application for a Ballot by Mail
glance_notes.text: Voting by Mail Requires Eligibility: Texas does not provide no-excuse voting by mail. A voter must qualify under one of the categories established by state law. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the early voting clerk must receive a regular ballot-by-mail application by October 23.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: To register to vote in Texas, a person must be a U.S. citizen, be a resident of the Texas county where the application is submitted, be at least 18 years old on Election Day, not be finally convicted of a felony unless the sentence has been fully completed or the person has been pardoned or otherwise released from the resulting disability to vote, and not have been declared by a court exercising probate jurisdiction to be totally mentally incapacitated or partially mentally incapacitated without the right to vote. A person who is at least 17 years and 10 months old may submit a registration application in advance of becoming eligible. Texas does not offer a general standalone online voter-registration system. Eligible residents may register through certain Texas Department of Public Safety transactions or complete, sign and submit a voter registration application to their county voter registrar.
register.glance_value: Paper registration or qualifying DPS transaction; no general standalone online registration
register.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — Voter Registration
register.internal_note: Texas should not be described simply as having online voter registration. New voters can register during qualifying DPS driver's license or ID transactions, including certain online DPS transactions, but Texas does not operate a general standalone online voter-registration portal. A person with a final felony conviction becomes eligible after successfully completing the punishment, including incarceration, parole, supervision or probation, or after being pardoned or otherwise released from the disability to vote.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use the Texas Secretary of State's Am I Registered? system to check your voter registration and obtain voter-specific election information. The system can provide registration status, county election information, polling-place information and other details as they become available. Voters should confirm their registration and voting location before the election, particularly after moving.
check_registration.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — Am I Registered?
check_registration.internal_note: Texas's voter lookup is commonly called Am I Registered? or My Voter Portal. County-specific polling-place and ballot information may not be populated until closer to the election.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Texas generally requires voter registration by the 30th day before an election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the 30th day is Sunday, October 4, so the deadline is extended to Monday, October 5. Texas does not provide general Election Day or same-day voter registration. Voters submitting a paper application should follow the state's mailing or delivery requirements and confirm that their registration has been accepted.
deadlines.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — November 3, 2026 Election Law Calendar
deadlines.internal_note: The official 2026 calendar expressly identifies October 5 as the final registration day. Section 13.143(e) moves the deadline from Sunday, October 4 to the next business day.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use the Texas Secretary of State's Am I Registered? system or your county election office to find voting locations. During early voting, a registered voter may vote at any early-voting location in the voter's county of registration. Election Day procedures depend on the county: counties using the Countywide Polling Place Program allow voters to use any participating Election Day vote center in the county, while other counties assign voters to specific precinct polling places. Voters should check their county's current information before Election Day.
polling_place.glance_value: Check Am I Registered? or your county election office
polling_place.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — Am I Registered?
polling_place.internal_note: Do not tell every Texas voter they must use one assigned precinct on Election Day. Texas permits approved counties to operate countywide polling-place programs. Early voting is simpler: any registered voter may use any early-voting location in the county of registration. Reverify county locations close to Election Day.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Texas's General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polls are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. local time. A voter who is in line at 7:00 p.m. may remain in line and vote. Voters voting in person generally must present one of Texas's accepted forms of photo identification. A registered voter who does not possess an accepted photo ID and cannot reasonably obtain one may use the state's Reasonable Impediment Declaration procedure and present an accepted supporting document.
election_day.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — November 3, 2026 Election Law Calendar
election_day.internal_note: The official November 2026 Election Law Calendar directly establishes 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. Election Day polling hours. Texas spans two time zones, so retain 'local time.' Identification requirements include the Reasonable Impediment Declaration procedure and additional procedures for voters who do not present qualifying identification.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Texas polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. local time on Election Day. A voter who is in line when the polls close at 7:00 p.m. is entitled to vote.
polling_hours.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — November 3, 2026 Election Law Calendar
polling_hours.internal_note: Texas has counties in both Central and Mountain Time. State law uses 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. at the location of the election, so local time is the clearest wording.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Any registered Texas voter may vote early in person without providing a reason. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting by personal appearance begins Monday, October 19 and ends Friday, October 30. A voter may use any early-voting location in the voter's county of registration. Hours and locations vary by county. For this General Election, the main early-voting location must operate for at least nine hours on each weekday during the first week, at least 12 hours on Saturday, October 24, at least six hours on Sunday, October 25, and at least 12 consecutive hours on each weekday from October 26 through October 30. Voters should check their county's official schedule for exact locations and hours.
early_voting.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — November 3, 2026 Election Law Calendar
early_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State's 2026 calendar provides unusually detailed minimum hours. Week 1, October 19-23: at least nine hours daily at the main site. Saturday October 24: at least 12 consecutive hours. Sunday October 25: at least six consecutive hours. October 26-30: at least 12 consecutive hours each weekday. County schedules may exceed these minimums. Branch-site requirements differ depending on county population and local arrangements.

absentee_mail.label: Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Texas does not provide no-excuse voting by mail. A registered voter may qualify to vote by mail if the voter will be 65 or older on Election Day, is sick or disabled under Texas law, expects to give birth within three weeks before or after Election Day, expects to be outside the county of residence during the entire early-voting period and on Election Day, or is confined in jail or involuntary civil commitment while otherwise eligible to vote. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the early voting clerk must receive an Application for Ballot by Mail by October 23. The regular Election Day receipt deadline is 7:00 p.m. November 3. A domestic ballot received after that time may still qualify if it was placed for delivery by 7:00 p.m. Election Day, bears the required postal or carrier mark and is received by 5:00 p.m. November 4. Different deadlines apply to qualifying military and overseas ballots.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Eligibility required; application received by October 23
absentee_mail.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — Application for a Ballot by Mail
absentee_mail.internal_note: Texas's official materials list five principal ballot-by-mail categories: age 65+, sickness/disability, absence from county, expected childbirth within three weeks before or after Election Day, and confinement in jail or involuntary civil commitment while otherwise eligible. October 23 is a RECEIVED deadline, not a postmark deadline. The November 4 late-domestic-ballot rule requires a qualifying cancellation or receipt mark showing placement for delivery by 7:00 p.m. Election Day. A voter may personally deliver the voter's marked mail ballot to the early voting clerk's office only on Election Day while polls are open and must present acceptable identification.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Texas voters voting in person generally present one of seven accepted forms of photo identification: a Texas driver license, Texas Election Identification Certificate, Texas personal identification card, Texas handgun license, U.S. military identification card containing the voter's photograph, U.S. citizenship certificate containing the voter's photograph, or U.S. passport. A registered voter who does not possess one of the accepted photo IDs and cannot reasonably obtain one may complete a Reasonable Impediment Declaration and present an accepted supporting document, such as a voter registration certificate, certified birth certificate, current utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck or qualifying government document. Additional provisional-ballot procedures are available in some circumstances.
voter_id.glance_value: Photo ID generally required; reasonable-impediment procedure available
voter_id.source_name: VoteTexas.gov — Required Identification for Voting in Person
voter_id.internal_note: Do not describe Texas's voter-ID rule as absolute. The Reasonable Impediment Declaration is a significant statutory alternative for a registered voter who does not possess and cannot reasonably obtain an accepted photo ID. Age-related expiration rules apply to some photo IDs. Certain voters with disabilities may obtain a permanent exemption from the photo-ID requirement through their county voter registrar.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Texas provides accessible voting options and assistance for voters with disabilities. Polling places must provide accessible voting equipment as required by state and federal law, subject to limited statutory exemptions. A voter who needs assistance because of a physical disability, inability to read or inability to understand the language on the ballot may receive assistance from an eligible person of the voter's choice, subject to legal restrictions. Texas also provides curbside voting for a voter who is physically unable to enter the polling place without personal assistance or likelihood of injury to the voter's health. Qualifying voters with disabilities may also be eligible to vote by mail.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible equipment, assistance, curbside voting and mail options
accessible_voting.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — Voting System Accessibility Requirements
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State issued 2026 guidance specifically addressing statutory exemptions to voting-system accessibility requirements, so avoid saying without qualification that every individual Texas polling location always has a particular accessible machine. Texas Election Code also provides curbside voting for qualifying voters physically unable to enter a polling place. County election officials should be contacted for voter-specific accessibility arrangements.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Texas provides special voting procedures for eligible active-duty military members, qualifying spouses and dependents, members of the Merchant Marine, qualifying National Guard and reserve members, and U.S. citizens living overseas. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request a ballot and may use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot as a backup when eligible. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the FPCA deadline is October 23, and election officials must send ballots to covered FPCA voters by September 19. A voter may request electronic delivery of an unmarked ballot. Marked ballots generally cannot be returned by email and must be physically returned, although a narrow exception applies to certain military voters and their spouses or dependents in qualifying combat-zone or hostile-fire circumstances. Receipt deadlines vary by voter category and method of application; for the 2026 General Election, qualifying overseas and military FPCA ballots may be received through November 9 under applicable state law.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA deadline October 23; electronic ballot delivery available
military_overseas.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — 2026 MOVE Act Military & Overseas Voting Guidance
military_overseas.internal_note: Texas's UOCAVA deadlines are category-specific. The 2026 Election Law Calendar establishes November 9 as the applicable extended receipt date because the ordinary fifth day after Election Day falls on Sunday. Military FPCA voters receive the statutory sixth-day deadline, also November 9 in 2026. Nonmilitary overseas FPCA ballots generally must be placed for delivery by Election Day. Marked ballots may NOT ordinarily be emailed. Election Advisory 2026-04 confirms the narrow email-return exception for active-duty military voters and qualifying spouses/dependents stationed in recognized hostile-fire, imminent-danger-pay or combat zones.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Texas if they meet the state's voter eligibility and residency requirements and establish a Texas residence for voting purposes. A student should register at the residence the student considers home for voting and may vote in only one jurisdiction in an election. Students who remain registered at a Texas address away from school may use early voting when they are in their county or may qualify to vote by mail if they will be outside their county of residence throughout the entire in-person early-voting period and on Election Day. A Texas college or university student identification card by itself is not one of the seven primary forms of photo identification accepted for in-person voting.
student_voting.glance_value: Use your qualifying voting residence; ordinary student ID is not a primary Texas voter ID
student_voting.source_name: VoteTexas.gov — Required Identification for Voting in Person
student_voting.internal_note: Texas does not list ordinary college student IDs among the seven accepted primary photo IDs. Students who lack accepted photo ID may still qualify for the Reasonable Impediment Declaration process if they cannot reasonably obtain one and possess an accepted supporting document. Do not imply that attending a Texas college automatically establishes Texas voting residency.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Texas ballots vary by county, precinct and political districts. Voters should use the Secretary of State's voter-information system and their county election office to find voter-specific ballot information and official sample ballots when available. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the Texas Secretary of State also publishes statewide candidate information, but local races and measures depend on the voter's residence.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Check your county election office for your voter-specific sample ballot
sample_ballot.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — Am I Registered?
sample_ballot.internal_note: Texas does not have one sample ballot that applies statewide because county, district and local contests vary. The Secretary of State's November 2026 election page provides statewide candidate information, while county election authorities provide voter-specific ballots. Reverify after final General Election ballots are published.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Texas Secretary of State, Elections Division. Mailing address: P.O. Box 12060, Austin, TX 78711-2060. Physical address: James E. Rudder Building, 1019 Brazos Street, Austin, TX 78701. Toll-free voter assistance: 1-800-252-VOTE (8683). Phone: 512-463-5650. Email: elections@sos.texas.gov. Office hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Central Time, Monday through Friday. For voter-specific registration, polling-place, early-voting or ballot-by-mail questions, contact the appropriate county election office.
contact.source_name: Texas Secretary of State — Elections Division Contact Information
contact.internal_note: The Elections Division's current contact page verifies the mailing and physical addresses, 1-800-252-VOTE, 512-463-5650 and office hours. Current Secretary of State election materials identify [elections@sos.texas.gov](mailto:elections@sos.texas.gov) as the Elections Division email. The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Texas Secretary of State Elections Division, VoteTexas.gov, the Am I Registered? voter portal and your county election office for official election information. These resources provide voter registration requirements, registration lookup, polling and early-voting locations, voter identification requirements, ballot-by-mail information, military and overseas voting guidance, election dates and voter-specific county information. Texas elections are administered locally by county election officials under state election law.
